# Chemist
You fight with chemistry. Your launcher lobs clouds that make the squad stronger and the horde weaker, and the fighting itself keeps it loaded.
## The chem launcher
You start with it in hand. Click to lob a canister - it lands where you aim, or bursts early on the first mob it hits on the side it is meant for, and leaves a cloud for a few seconds.
- [bold]Support[/bold] formulas only touch crew. Stand your squad in the cloud, or put it at their feet. - [bold]Hostile[/bold] formulas only touch zombies. They never hurt crew or player structures.
The launcher carries three formulas at once. Press [bold]Z[/bold] with it in hand to pick which one fires next. Every shot spends reserve; the gauge on the left of your HUD shows how much is left.
## Keeping it loaded
You never walk back to refill. Every wave enemy that dies near you, to anyone's gun, tops up the reserve - tougher enemies give more. The reserve also fills to the brim when prep starts, so every wave begins loaded.
## Formulas
Ready from the start:
- [bold]Combat Stim[/bold] - crew hit harder, swing and shoot faster, and move quicker for 20 seconds. - [bold]Mending Mist[/bold] - stops bleeding and heals crew while they stand in it. - [bold]Corrosive[/bold] - burns every zombie in the cloud. The damage and the kills count as yours. - [bold]Weakening Agent[/bold] - zombies take 25% more damage from everyone for a while. - [bold]Solvent[/bold] - strips armoured zombies' plating for good.
The CMO can research [bold]Etchant[/bold], [bold]Adrenal Surge[/bold], [bold]Battle Analgesic[/bold] and [bold]Binding Agent[/bold] on the medical console. They show up at the bench as soon as they are bought - nothing to print.
Buffs last 20 seconds and refresh every time a cloud touches someone, so keep the clouds coming. Your health-bar view marks crew with a buff and how long it has left, and flags the ones without one.
## Catalyst
Buffing crewmates, damaging zombies and assisting kills fills your catalyst meter. When it is full, press the Über key (Alt+E by default) to arm it: your next canister makes a bigger cloud that lasts longer, and hostile and mending clouds hit harder. Research picks what a catalysed cloud does on top - [bold]Chain Reaction[/bold] makes hostile clouds burst and spread to dying zombies, [bold]Panacea[/bold] makes support clouds heal hard.
## The field kit station
The [bold]Loadout[/bold] tab sets which formulas your launcher carries. Pick a slot, then a formula. You can change it any time, but you never have to come back mid-wave.
During prep, brew a [bold]wave tonic[/bold] there. Carry the urn to where the squad gathers; each crewmate drinks once for a small bonus that lasts the whole wave.
The [bold]Pharmacy[/bold] tab is a dispenser for doctors: dispense into a jug, then press labelled bottles or pills.
## Getting paid
- Your clouds' damage earns hit money like any gun, and their kills are yours. - A zombie you weakened, stripped or burned that someone else kills pays you an assist. - A crewmate you buffed scoring a kill pays you a cut. - Crewmates drinking your tonic pay you. - A doctor using your pills or bottles pays you a share.
Dosing yourself pays nothing. Being where the squad is pays everything.
